title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten French page written on the back of a typed English translation; the typed text is a Kodaira-type vanishing/embedding argument and is unrelated. The handwriting belongs to the motivic Galois theory notes and appears to treat motives over a finite field F_q of characteristic p.

Step 1. The top line sketches an extension: Z_l (or a quotient of it) -> Gamma -> Gamma' -> 0, with a subgroup Gamma_p (1 -> Gamma_p) marked beneath. This looks like the Galois or Weil group of F_q and its p-part, related to the lattice (Z^p)'.

Step 2. 'D'autre part' (on the other hand), the lattice (Z^p)' corresponds to an algebraic torus over Q, described through Galois theory:
- Take L_0, a quadratic extension of K_0. In context this is a CM field over its totally real subfield.
- L_0/K_0 defines a one-dimensional torus U = Ker(Res_{L_0/K_0} G_m --Norm--> G_{m,K_0}), the norm-one (unitary) torus.
- Set G' = Res_{K_0/Q} U = Ker(Res_{L_0/Q} G_m -> Res_{K_0/Q} G_m), so G'(Q) = Ker(N_{L_0/K_0}: L_0^* -> K_0^*).

Step 3. This gives (**) phi: G' -> G, an isogeny of G' onto G. Here G is the torus with character group (Z^p)'; plausibly it is the torus generated by the normalized Frobenius, a motivic Galois group of the relevant motive over F_q.

Step 4. The cocharacter nu: G_{m,L_0} -> G_{L_0} factors through G'_{L_0}. A commutative square relates nu' on a restriction-of-scalars torus to nu.

Step 5. Warning: the element f_0 = f * g(p^{1/2}) of G(Q) does NOT in general lift through phi to an element f' of G'(Q). Here f_0 is Frobenius f normalized by a factor involving p^{1/2}, i.e. roughly pi/sqrt(q). The lift is possible only if one has chosen a basis, i.e. an isomorphism M(q)/torsion ≅ (Z^p)', where M(q) is the group of Weil q-numbers.

Interpretation. A Weil q-number pi lies in a CM field L_0 with pi * pi-bar = q. So pi/sqrt(q) has norm 1 but generally lives in L_0(sqrt q), not in L_0. The page thus shows Grothendieck computing the Tannakian (motivic) group of motives over F_q as a torus dual to Weil q-numbers modulo torsion, realised up to isogeny as a product of CM norm-one tori. He also notices the obstruction caused by sqrt(p): Frobenius does not descend to a Q-point. This is the germ of the Weil-number torus P and of the non-neutrality over Q of motives over F_q.
errors: Not a logical error, but the text is ambiguous: G is never defined on the page. The isogeny phi: G' -> G is asserted without saying which character lattice G carries.
The claim that f_0 fails to lift is stated without proof. It is correct in general (sqrt(q) need not lie in L_0, and phi need not be surjective on Q-points), but no justification is given.

ideas.what: The motivic Galois group of (CM / abelian-variety) motives over F_q is a torus whose character group is the group of Weil q-numbers modulo torsion
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number torus P (kernel of the motivic Galois group over F_q)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (thesis, 1972, ch. VI, under Grothendieck); Langlands–Rapoport 1987; Milne 1994 'Motives over finite fields'
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (LNM 265)

ideas.what: Description of the relevant torus via the norm-one torus Ker(Res_{L0/K0} G_m -> G_m) of a CM extension, restricted to Q
ideas.modern_name: unitary/norm-one torus of a CM field; tori of CM type

ideas.what: Normalized Frobenius pi/sqrt(q) is not a Q-point of the lifted torus G'; the obstruction comes from sqrt(p) and the choice of basis of the Weil-number lattice
ideas.modern_name: sqrt(q)/sign problem; non-neutrality of motives over F_q over Q (Weil-number gerbe)

missed.claim: Early (possibly 1965) explicit computation by Grothendieck of the Frobenius torus over F_q as an isogenous image of a product of CM norm-one tori. It includes the observation that normalized Frobenius need not lift because of p^{1/2}. This anticipates the Weil-number torus and the obstruction later studied by Langlands–Rapoport and Milne.
missed.quote: On fera attention que l'élément f_0 de G(Q) [= f g(p^{1/2})] ne se relève pas en un élément f' de G'(Q) par φ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own priority and viewpoint on motives over finite fields and the sqrt(q) issue, usually attributed to Saavedra and later Langlands–Rapoport and Milne. It is historiographical rather than mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: It is historically interesting to see Grothendieck himself, possibly in 1965, handling the Weil-number torus and the sqrt(p) obstruction to lifting Frobenius. The mathematics itself is now standard (Saavedra, Milne), and the dating is uncertain.

'définit un groupe[?] tore[?]' likely 'définit un tore'.
'R_{?} G_{m,L_0}' in the diagram is probably a restriction-of-scalars symbol (Res/R) rather than an unknown.
'G(Q)^*' appears as 'G(Q)' with a superscript annotation, probably 'ou' or '^ou'; the inserted '= f g(p^{1/2})' is a marginal addition attached to f_0.
'– donc une[?] base[?]' is probably 'd'où un homom.' introducing (**).
